fronts.question: For Sergeev's TR20-096 container construction, Theorem 2 sets s = ceil(2 gamma log a) and states the bound P_m(a) >= 2^{a+1/2} - O(a^{-gamma} 2^a) only 'when, for example, gamma <= 1/5'. Is every gamma < 1/4 admissible, yielding S(n) <= log2(n!) + O(n / (log n)^gamma) for all n, or does some error term force a hard exponent cap at 1/5?
fronts.falsifier: A careful re-derivation exhibiting an error term, for instance exp(-Theta(a s^{-2} 2^{-2s})) or the lambda <= 1/50 condition, that blocks every gamma > 1/5 would refute the improvement; an explicit gamma > 1/5 derivation with all constants checked would refute the 1/5 cap.
fronts.implication: An admissible gamma closer to 1/4 would sharpen the uniform upper envelope on the exact value S(n) and shrink the k-range a unary threshold decider must search; it is not by itself a faster evaluator or a class placement, and it would strengthen schedule-level surplus estimates used by the newest #301 framed-DAG barrier.
fronts.basis: Primary TR20-096 p.28-29: phi > 0 requires only gamma <= 1/4 while the final bound is stated 'when, for example, gamma <= 1/5'; p.29 Corollary 2 fixes 1/5. Direct arithmetic gives 2^{-s/2} = a^{-gamma} and 2^{-2s} = a^{-4gamma}, so the exponential error term appears negligible for gamma < 1/4; this is a textual and arithmetic observation, not a proof.

fronts.question: Fix any legal parameter choice in Sergeev's TR20-096 pair-sort plus group-insertion schedule and let C_A(n) be its worst-case comparison count. Is C_A(n) - log2(n!) >= c n / (log n)^{1/5} with an explicit c > 0 for all large n, or can a refinement of the same architecture drive the schedule's surplus to o(n / (log n)^{1/5})?
fronts.falsifier: Exhibit a legal fixed schedule whose surplus is o(n/(log n)^{1/5}), refuting the rate lower bound; or derive explicit c > 0 and n0 certifying the Omega(n/(log n)^{1/5}) schedule bound for every n >= n0, refuting the refinement reading. Neither branch yields a claim about the optimum S(n).
fronts.implication: An explicit schedule-level rate lower bound is the missing ingredient named in the newest #301 sergeev-framed-dag-exact-budget-alln finding: paired with any effective upper bound on S(n)'s surplus it would force that architecture's height above S(n) infinitely often; the opposite answer would weaken the barrier and improve explicit upper bounds, without placing SORT-BOUND-U in a class.
fronts.basis: Newest board #301 sergeev-framed-dag-exact-budget-alln FINDING 3 states a surplus lower bound for a fixed schedule is absent from TR20-096 and needed for its falsifier; Theorem 3 (pp.29-30) supplies only an unquantified O(n log^{-1/5} n) upper bound. I independently recomputed Lemma 4's lambda(s) = 20*2^{-s/2} + 64*2^{-s}, first below 1 at s = 10; no all-n schedule rate is claimed.
